newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU's Bjerregaard to try for fast decision on corn.
newsitem.headline: EU's Bjerregaard to try for fast decision on corn.

text.p: Environment Commissioner Ritt Bjerregaard will push on Wednesday for scientists to report before the end of October on the safety of Ciba Geigy's genetically modified maize, a Commission spokesman said on Tuesday.
The move is an attempt to speed up an EU decision on whether a gene-modified maize produced by Swiss chemical company Ciba Geigy is safe for cultivation by EU farmers.
"She's pushing for these assessments to be made as speedily as possible," the spokesman told reporters on the margins of Tuesday's Environment Council.
He could not say when the Commission would reach a final decision under Directive 90/220/EEC on whether or not to approve the corn strain.
Bjerregaard told the Council that she would urge fellow Commissioners to back her call for urgency during Wednesday's regular weekly meeting in Brussels, he said.

Delays to the EU's approval process have raised the prospect of trade friction with the United States, whose farmers plan to export the same maize strain to EU once they have completed this year's harvest.
The Ciba corn has been modified to be resistant to certain pesticides and to the European corn borer pest, which destroys significant parts of the European harvest.

Some EU countries, such as Austria and Sweden, are worried that not enough is known about the possible effects of releasing such products to the environment and fear pesticide-resistant plants may return as "super weeds" when other crops are grown.
